title: 3 pose as cops, gang-rape Delhi teen near Kalkaji Mandir
content: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men posing as police officers. The incident occurred in a park near Kalkaji Mandir after the girl and her friend visited the temple. Police received a PCR call and reached the spot, taking the girl for medical examination. Authorities are scanning CCTV footage and gathering information to identify the accused.

title: Is not singing Vande Mataram punishable offence? Supreme Court to examine
content: The Supreme Court will not decide on the National Song's stanza length now.  It will examine if not singing it can be a punishable offense.  The court referenced a past ruling stating no one can be punished for not singing the National Anthem.  The Centre opposed the challenge, citing a "naxalite mindset" for questioning the song.  The court asked the Centre to file its response to the public interest litigation.

title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu to engineers: Use AI but never cede
content: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu cautions engineers about excessive AI use in software creation. He advises using AI tools without losing essential understanding of the development process. An engineer described AI generating nearly all software components, causing team dissatisfaction. This rapid adoption of AI tools outpaces industry comprehension, inviting potential disaster. Engineers are working long hours directing AI, leading to a soul-sucking experience.

title: Swept away by raging Teesta in Bengal, elephant calf saved by four fishermen
content: Five fishermen bravely rescued a newborn elephant calf from the Teesta river.  They spotted the calf struggling and pulled it onto their small row boat.  Forest personnel provided immediate veterinary care to the distressed young elephant.  Efforts were then made to reunite the calf with its mother.  After two hours, the calf was successfully reunited and seen nursing.

title: Wife sold Rs 25 soft drink for Rs 26; husband faced case for 13 years, HC quashes it
content: The court has quashed the prosecution, which arose from an allegation that the man had sold a 600-ml bottle of cold drink for Rs 26 even though its MRP was Rs 25. The allegation concerned an overcharge of Re 1. The man was working at his wife's shop when the incident took place.

title: Ohio attorney bought 155 neglected acres; 38 years later, family farms nearly 500
content: In 1988, Ohio attorney Neil McKown quietly purchased 155 acres without first telling his wife, Pamela. The property was overgrown, rundown and neglected, but what initially looked like a risky decision eventually became the foundation of a nearly 500-acre family farming operation.

title: Florida used robot rabbits to hunt Burmese pythons threatening the Everglades
content: Florida is testing solar-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades. Developed by the South Florida Water Management District and University of Florida, the robotic decoys mimic prey using heat and scent while AI cameras detect approaching snakes. Officials can then alert trained removal agents, adding technology to Florida’s wider python control efforts.

title: Meet Abhishek Anand, from IIT Kanpur and IT job to Japan’s cricket team
content: Abhishek Anand, a former resident of Rohtas, has successfully transitioned to playing for Japan's national cricket team after relocating for work. Utilizing his time at a local club, Anand dedicated three years to honing his skills, ultimately meeting the residency and passport criteria for selection. His journey represents the growing presence of Bihari and Jharkhandi professionals thriving in Japan's technology landscape.

title: From Op Sindoor to Urgent Fury, how network warfare has changed the way conflicts are fought
content: Network-centric warfare is reshaping how wars are fought and won today. India faces significant security challenges across multiple domains simultaneously. Existing Indian defense networks like AFNET and DCN are crucial for integration. These systems enable faster battlefield decisions and shared operational pictures. Companies are actively developing capabilities for this evolving warfare.

title: 585kg waste gone in 4.5 hrs, Bittu Tabahi takes cleanliness mission to Delhi’s Yamuna
content: On September 20, Surendra Singh Choudhary, affectionately called Bittu Tabahi, spearheaded a remarkable cleanup initiative along the banks of the Yamuna river. In a dedicated four-hour effort, he and a team of volunteers successfully gathered an impressive 585 kilograms of litter. This endeavor was part of World Cleanup Day, supported by Philip Morris.

title: TOI-DPA Airfare Index: A flight price tracker that will help you plan trips better
content: The TOI-DPA Airline Price Index monitors daily fluctuations in domestic airfares across India, illuminating trends in inflation, demand, and pricing strategies for various routes. Additionally, the Fare Timing Index reveals how ticket prices adjust over time related to booking. Factors such as departure times and specific days of the week play a critical role in determining fare costs, leading to valuable insights into airline pricing dynamics.

title: Will AI 'kill' all humans? Decoding the conspiracy theories
content: In this edition of Random Musing, we decline Pascal’s wager and instead assume Pascal’s mugging and look at three conspiracy theories that are starting to feel less like conspiracy theories: 1) The China Boat, 2) The Shylock Problem, and 3) The Guardrail Cartel.

title: 40-year-old man dies after Thar hits scooter in Greater Noida, wife injured
content: A 40-year-old man died and his wife was injured after a Thar SUV collided with their scooter. The accident occurred in the Bisrakh police station area on Monday. Neeraj succumbed to his injuries during treatment at a hospital. Police have taken the Thar SUV into custody and are searching for the driver. Legal proceedings are underway after obtaining a complaint from the victim's family.

title: Delhi trekker found dead in 400m gorge in Ukhand’s Chopta while trying to take photo
content: A woman from Delhi tragically lost her life during a solo trip to Chopta when she slipped and fell into a deep gorge while trying to capture photographs. After her family reported her missing when she didn't return, rescue teams initiated a search operation that ultimately led to the discovery of her body. Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding this heartbreaking incident.

title: Meet UP’s Green Army: Women fighting violence, addiction and child marriage
content: In Uttar Pradesh, women don green saris and wield lathis, forming the Green Army to tackle pressing village issues like gambling, alcohol misuse, and domestic violence. Drawing strength from their personal experiences, they advocate for girls' education and fight against child marriages. Their initiatives also include celebrating daughters' births and supporting sustainable livelihoods, fostering significant social transformation in rural areas.

title: MakeMyTrip ordered to pay Rs 48,775 after two booked hotels found non-existent
content: A consumer commission ordered MakeMyTrip to refund Rs 18,775 for non-existent hotels. The complainant booked two properties which were not found at their listed locations. This led to the family sleeping in their car in sub-zero temperatures. MakeMyTrip was held liable for listing misrepresented and non-existent properties. The commission also awarded compensation and litigation costs to the aggrieved consumer.

title: Can you reshape a newborn’s nose with your fingers? Doctor debunks viral claim
content: A traditional practice suggests that pressing a baby's nose each day can help shape it more sharply over time. Nevertheless, doctors assert that this method does not effectively change the nose's structure. Unlike the skull, the cartilage in a nose remains pliable and does not possess internal rigidity. For a lasting change in nose shape, surgical procedures are necessary.

title: How Puducherry offers housing sites to homeless and underprivileged communities
content: Puducherry is extending its generous initiative that provides free house plots to economically disadvantaged families and those belonging to scheduled caste communities. Since its inception in 1981, the scheme supports individuals who do not have land for housing. Eligible applicants must be Indian citizens with a yearly family income below Rs 24,000 and need to present a range of documents including identity, residence, income, and caste certificates.

title: Naga teen on way to buy essentials killed in Manipur ambush
content: A 17-year-old Naga boy was killed in an alleged ambush by suspected Kuki militants.  This incident occurred in Manipur's Tamenglong district on Monday morning.  Tensions between the Naga and Kuki communities have escalated following this event.  Five Kuki villagers were also killed in separate incidents involving suspected Naga militants.  Several houses were torched in Naga and Kuki-inhabited areas across the state.

title: 91-year-old woman dies after monkey attacks, pushes her in Karnataka
content: A 91-year-old woman named Najamunisa Begum died on Monday in Koppal district. She was allegedly attacked and pushed by a monkey while standing outside her home. The injured woman was immediately rushed to a hospital for urgent medical treatment. Sadly, she later succumbed to her severe injuries sustained during the incident. Authorities are currently investigating the precise circumstances surrounding this unfortunate monkey attack.

title: Why are girls’ shorts shorter than boys’ at 18 months? Moms raise questions
content: A digital creator recently showcased the varying designs of toddler shorts, intended for kids aged eighteen months. The differences in cut sparked discussions among parents, who are prioritizing comfort and practicality rather than adhering to traditional gender stereotypes. They are selecting clothing from diverse sections to ensure a better fit and greater freedom for their active toddlers, highlighting the shift towards functionality over labels.

title: ‘Global order under stress’: Jaishankar calls for stronger multilateralism at UNGA
content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar called for stronger multilateralism at a UNGA summit. He stressed greater international cooperation to address conflicts and emerging technologies. India also co-chaired the first Partners for Multilateralism summit in New York. Slovakia backed India's bid for a permanent UN Security Council seat. The Visegrad Group plus India meeting marked a new historic occasion.

title: Inevitable veto power? 4 European nations back India’s permanent UN seat bid
content: The V4 comprises Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia. The four countries held their first ministerial-level meeting with India in the new V4+India format during the UNGA high-level week. Jaishankar described the meeting as a "new historic occasion" and said the discussions covered political, economic, defence, technology, space, connectivity and people-to-people ties.

title: 5-day-old infant dies after fire breaks out at Telangana's RIMS hospital; 28 newborns rescued
content: Tragedy struck at RIMS Hospital in Adilabad when a five-day-old newborn sadly lost their life due to a fire that broke out late Monday night. Fortunately, twenty-eight children were safely evacuated from the affected ward. The flames ignited around 11:50 pm, leading to a swift response from fire services. Firefighters managed to control the situation, while police have since registered a case and are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.

title: Marriage plans in doubt, Hyderabad cop ends life after video call with fiancee

The constable reportedly called his fiancée before taking the extreme step.  Police are probing the exact cause of his death.  He was under distress after learning his marriage might not happen.

title: US airports resume operations after telecom outage disrupts thousands of flights
content: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the communications lines had been repaired and operations were gradually resuming, although passengers were still expected to face delays as airlines worked through the backlog. "The telecom lines have been repaired, and all airport operations in the Northeast are resuming," Duffy said. The outage meant that flights headed for some of the airports could not land.

Students are actively protesting for more decisive actions and the formation of an independent inquiry committee. The grieving family accuses the institute of abetment and harassment, seeking a CID-led investigation, as campus tensions mount.

title: Why do students study more under pressure but remember less?
content: Every exam season, the same scene repeats itself in homes across India. Lights stay on past midnight, notebooks pile up, and a student who has barely looked at a chapter all year suddenly spends twelve hours a day buried in it. And yet, when results come in, the outcome is often disappointing. Not because the child didn't work hard enough, but because working harder under panic and working smart under calm are two completely different things and we keep confusing one for the other.

title: Drones carrying ground robots: Ukraine’s new battlefield tactic against Russia
content: Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi expanded drone use with ground vehicles deployed by aerial bombers.  These unmanned ground vehicles targeted Russian logistic nodes deep within occupied territory.  Ukrainian forces recaptured significant territory using a layered approach with robotics and electronic warfare.  Unmanned ground vehicles now serve critical logistics, engineering, and infantry support roles.  This offensive highlights the deep integration of robotic systems into Ukraine's combat strategy.

title: 'No burden for consumers': Sitharaman clarifies who will pay MDR on UPI transactions
content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman addressed concerns over the Merchant Discount Rate charges, emphasizing that UPI users will face no additional financial burden. These charges apply solely to payment operators and do not treat consumers as taxpayers. The revised rule targets only high-value Person-to-Merchant UPI transactions, meaning most users will transact without incurring extra fees. The government has expressed its commitment to this decision, ruling out any changes.

content: Bessent's threat went beyond the airlines themselves but also targeted airports, ticketing companies, fuel suppliers, and other support businesses that help air carriers operate abroad.

title: Grounds in writing a must during arrests even in UAPA: Supreme Court
content: a bench of justices said a person must be provided with the grounds of arrest by the probe agency at the time of arrest in writing and its language understandable to the accused . the bench said this is applicable in all cases including under special laws - such as PMLA and UAPA .

title: Watch: Press pool boycott leaves Trump barely audible at White House event
content: president was barely audible during live coverage of a white house event on Monday . he unveiled a new helipad on the white house South Lawn and spoke with construction workers . but the sound of Marine One drowned out much of his speech .

title: 'No complaint received by SC/ST cell from Sahil': IIT-B prof on student suicide case
content: professor Suryanarayana Doolla's cell had no record of the student approaching it with a complaint in the months preceding his death . he said the institute's SC/ST cell had issued a notice stating that there had been no attempt by Sahil to approach the cell in the previous three or four months .

title: 'Chhitputh ghatna': Bihar minister's outrageous remark on Jamui harassment video
content: the remarks came after the assault and groping of a girl came to light through a video that went viral on social media . an FIR has been registered in connection with the incident, while police have arrested three people and formed a special investigation team to identify and apprehend others involved .

title: Will shut Iranian flights from tomorrow: US new arm-twist move against Tehran
content: the warning comes as the Trump administration expands its sanctions campaign . the treasury secretary says Iranian airlines could "effectively be shut down around the world" he warns foreign companies providing services to Tehran's aviation sector with secondary sanctions .

title: ‘Indian yoga teachers’ row sparks debate as Australia tightens visa rules
content: Tony Burke, immigration minister, wants to draw a distinction between legitimate migration and vias-hopping . he said the government supported immigration as a contributor to Australia's economy but wanted greater control over a system that had historically relied heavily on demand-driven migration . Burke said that the government was bringing in more yoga teachers than construction workers .

title: US to reopen Cold War-era base, set up new military presence in Greenland: Report
content: the move is expected to be part of a new security agreement between the three sides . the sites are Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland, where the US operated the Bluie West One military base until the 1950s .
